findings.body:
**`cmd_selfcheck` now always succeeds. Its help text still promises a banned-identity check.**

The `selfcheck` help at Line 2786 still says "assert config carries no banned/third-party reviewer identity". The command now prints `ok` without checking anything. An operator or deploy step that runs `crq selfcheck` gets a passing result that the code does not support. The signer and spool checks could go with promotion, but the banned-identity check is independent of promotion. Restore that check. If the removal is intentional, change the help text so the command no longer claims the guarantee.
findings.title: `cmdselfcheck` now always succeeds. Its help text still promises a banned-identity check.

findings.body:
**Use `crq.verify_deferred_source` instead of the local `verify` closure.**

`crq.verify_deferred_source` at `apps/crq-python/crq.py:563-588` takes the same `(repo, pr)` arguments and returns the same keys. It also validates the forge identity before returning it. It checks that `base.repo.full_name` equals `REPO`, that `number` is an `int` equal to `pr`, that `head.sha` and `merge_commit_sha` are 40-character lowercase hex, that `merged` is a `bool`, and that `state` is `open` or `closed`. It returns `mergeSha` only for merged PRs. The closure at lines 48-53 returns `merge_commit_sha` for open PRs and performs none of these checks.

`queue_transport._forge` at `apps/crq-python/queue_transport.py:381-391` already checks repository, PR number, target branch, and, for deferred bindings, producer, head, and target. It does not check SHA format, the `merged` type, or the `open`/`closed` state. The validated source closes those gaps. Two copies of the forge identity logic can also drift apart, and one validator avoids that.

<details>
<summary>♻️ Proposed refactor</summary>

```diff
-        def verify(repo, pr):
-            source = crq.gh_json(["api", f"repos/{repo}/pulls/{pr}"])
-            return {"repo": source["base"]["repo"]["full_name"], "pr": source["number"],
-                    "producer": source["user"]["login"], "head": source["head"]["sha"],
-                    "target": source["base"]["ref"], "mergeSha": source.get("merge_commit_sha"),
-                    "state": "MERGED" if source.get("merged") else source["state"].upper()}
-
         read_only = queue_transport.decode(raw)["op"] in queue_transport.READ | {"inventory"}
         execute = (lambda work, runner: work(runner)) if read_only else supervised
         result = execute(lambda runner: queue_transport.handle(
-            raw, runner, principal=principal, policy=policy, verify_source=verify,
+            raw, runner, principal=principal, policy=policy, verify_source=crq.verify_deferred_source,
             receipt_root=crq.STATE / "receipts"), crq)
```

</details>
findings.title: Use `crq.verifydeferredsource` instead of the local `verify` closure.
